# Payment Method Events

A connected clause that announces account payment instructions and translates payment requests into MyOS execution-request events. It reads `/paymentDetails` and `/paymentDetails/method` from the document where it executes, including a nested instruction’s own document. These values are read when each action runs; no fallback method is defined.

- **`announce`** automatically runs on `Clauses Initialized`, which represents successful initial clause installation. Its automatic connection has `once: true`. When `/paymentDetails/method` is not equal to `myos-customer`, it appends a `Payment Event` with `kind: Account Payment Instruction Created` and `details` copied from `/paymentDetails`. For `myos-customer`, it emits no announcement. The one-time connection is still marked as fired after that action completes, so this marker does not prove an announcement was emitted.
- **`request`** automatically responds to an `Event` matching `kind: Payment Requested`. It appends a `Payment Event` with `kind: MyOS Execution Requested`, `details` copied from `/paymentDetails`, `method` copied from `/paymentDetails/method`, and `request` containing the full triggering event. This action also applies to `myos-customer`. Its automatic connection defaults to `once: false`, and the action body has no duplicate-request check.

These actions emit notifications and requests; they do not confirm external execution, transfer of funds, or payment completion, and their bodies do not update payment status.

Inherited configuration supports additional named action connections through `bindings`; `_automatic` is reserved for the built-in connections. A connection’s `when` defaults to `true` and skips execution when false. Optional `parameters.conditions.announce` and `parameters.conditions.request` also default to `true`, but a false action condition rejects execution with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`. Changing an installed clause’s configuration requires a new clause key.
